brief: Goldman Sachs macro traders Rikin Shah and Cosimo Codacci-Pisanelli argue energy is setting the path for rates. Qatari LNG through the Strait of Hormuz runs at 15%-25% of pre-war levels while Gulf oil exports have recovered to two-thirds of normal, so European winter storage needs price-driven LNG demand destruction outside Europe through end-2026 unless Qatar normalises. The beta of rates to energy is back at the highs and is called the primary driver of moves. Higher energy plus a leg higher in US rates plus a damp squib first Bessent buyback should therefore put markets near US reflexivity levels, with equity resilience the only missing piece, though the note flags AI capex and earnings growth as the other side. The 29bps core CPI print makes next week's Fed hike straightforward at 21.9bps priced, but the desk still expects a shallow cycle. ECB language and a greater than 50% October hike probability show reaction functions shifting with energy. UK front-end beta to gas is higher still, terminal pricing near 5%, and Bailey has not pivoted, which the note treats as high pivot risk, not a decided outcome. Receiving November at a full hike priced is its cleanest long-side trade.
